equation_request.abstract: In this paper we present a quantum algorithm solving the triangle finding problem in unweighted graphs with query complexity $\tilde{O}(n^{5/4})$, where $n$ denotes the number of vertices in the graph. This improves the previous upper bound $O(n^{9/7})=O(n^{1.285...})$ recently obtained by Lee, Magniez and Santha. Our result shows, for the first time, that in the quantum query complexity setting unweighted triangle finding is easier than its edge-weighted version, since for finding an edge-weighted triangle Belovs and Rosmanis proved that any quantum algorithm requires $\Omega(n^{9/7}/\sqrt{\log n})$ queries. Our result also illustrates some limitations of the non-adaptive learning graph approach used to obtain the previous $O(n^{9/7})$ upper bound since, even over unweighted graphs, any quantum algorithm for triangle finding obtained using this approach requires $\Omega(n^{9/7}/\sqrt{\log n})$ queries as well. To bypass the obstacles characterized by these lower bounds, our quantum algorithm uses combinatorial ideas exploiting the graph-theoretic properties of triangle finding, which cannot be used when considering edge-weighted graphs or the non-adaptive learning graph approach.

specification.problem: Triangle finding in an unweighted n-vertex graph in the quantum query model: decide whether the graph contains a triangle and output one if so. The abstract claims query complexity O~(n^{5/4}).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the stated query-complexity bounds, plus a standard-background Grover search primitive over vertex triples on a tiny instance (n=4). The paper's actual combinatorial algorithm is not reconstructed, and no circuit-level details are given.

symbols.meaning: number of vertices of the graph
unweighted graph with |V|=n, accessed via adjacency-matrix queries
triangle indicator function over vertex triples
quantum query complexity of triangle finding

equations.label: Claimed upper bound
equations.description: Query complexity of the new algorithm for unweighted triangle finding.

equations.label: Previous upper bound
equations.description: Previous bound by Lee, Magniez and Santha, which is improved.

equations.label: Edge-weighted lower bound
equations.description: Lower bound for edge-weighted triangle finding, attributed to Belovs and Rosmanis. It is also the bound for the non-adaptive learning graph approach.
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract. Because 5/4 < 9/7, the new upper bound is below this weighted lower bound.

equations.label: Triangle indicator
equations.latex: T(a,b,c)=x_{ab}\wedge x_{bc}\wedge x_{ac},\quad \exists\,\{a,b,c\}: T=1 \iff G \text{ has a triangle}
equations.description: Predicate defining a triangle in terms of edge queries.
equations.justification: Definition of a triangle; the abstract does not give it.

equations.label: Grover baseline (not the paper's method)
equations.description: Generic Grover search over triples with 3 edge queries per oracle call. It gives O(n^{3/2}) queries, worse than the claimed bound.
equations.justification: A simple baseline construction chosen for the tiny instance; it is not the abstract's algorithm.
assumptions: At most one marked triple, or known number of marked triples
Oracle evaluates T with 3 edge queries

registers.name: triple
registers.role: index of the candidate vertex triple

registers.name: edge_ancilla
registers.role: holds the queried edge bits for the oracle, then uncomputed

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over triple indices (assumed baseline); ancillas in |0>, phase qubit in |->.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition over the N candidate triples.
Apply the oracle O_T, which queries the three edges of each triple and flips the phase if all are present.
Apply the Grover diffusion operator and repeat O(sqrt(N)) times.
Compare the baseline cost with the claimed algorithm's cost.

specification.measurement: Measure the triple register in the computational basis, then classically verify the triple with 3 edge queries (baseline only).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Verify the candidate triangle; repeat if verification fails.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was provided; the smallest useful construction is a Grover baseline on n=4 vertices.
The Grover baseline is not the paper's algorithm and does not achieve O~(n^{5/4}).
The adjacency-matrix query model is assumed.
